name: Dominoes
description: Dominoes is a family of tile-based games played with rectangular 'domino' tiles. Each domino is a rectangular tile with a line dividing its face into two square ends. Each end is marked with a number of spots (also called pips, nips, or dobs) or is blank. The back of the dominoes in a set are indistinguishable, either blank or having some common design.

history.origins: Dominoes originated in China in the 12th century (documented in the 'Customs and Traditions of Chu-chiang'). They were brought to Italy in the 18th century, likely by missionaries, where they were modified into the European double-six set.
timeline: 1120 AD: Earliest reliable records of dominoes in China.
1700s: Dominoes appear in Italy (Venice and Naples).
1800s: Spreads to France and England, becoming a staple of pub culture.
Modern Era: Global popularity with high-level professional tournaments.
history.cultural: Used for both gaming and divination (especially in Asian cultures). In the West, it is a quintessential leisure game for all ages.
history.evolution: Chinese dominoes represent all possible outcomes of throwing two dice. European dominoes added 'blank' ends to create the standard double-six (28 tile) set.

setup.players: 2 to 4 players. Can be played in partnerships (2 vs 2).
setup.dealing: Tiles are shuffled face-down ('washing'). Players draw a hand (usually 7 tiles for 2 players, 5 for 3-4 players). Remaining tiles form the 'boneyard'.

rules.objective: Empty your hand of tiles or have the lowest total pip count when the game is blocked.
rules.gameplay:
1. Starting: The player with the highest double leads (usually the 6-6).
2. Matching: Players take turns placing a tile so that one end matches an open end of the line of play.
3. Drawing: In 'Draw' dominoes, if you cannot move, you must draw from the boneyard until a move is possible. In 'Block' dominoes, you simply pass.
4. Blocking: If no player can move and the boneyard is empty, the game is blocked.
keyRules: Doubles are usually played crosswise to the line.
The line can grow in two directions (standard) or four (spinners).
A 'Blocked' game winner is the player with the lowest pip total remaining.

strategy.basic: Keep as many suits in your hand as possible to ensure you have a legal move on every turn.
strategy.intermediate: Identify which suits your opponent is lacking (when they draw or pass) and try to 'starve' them of those suits.
strategy.advanced: Blocking: If you have a low total and suspect your opponent has high tiles, intentionally block the game to secure a win on points.
tips: Play your highest-value tiles early to reduce your risk if the game is blocked.
Control the ends of the line to force other players to draw from the boneyard.
